question: In 2022, the Official Journal of the EU published guidelines on well-functioning and sustainable local passenger transport-on-demand (taxis and occasional transport vehicles). Developments in the passenger transport-on-demand sector and the emergence of new market players and business models have also led to tensions and different legislative responses among Member States.

However, what is clear is that there is no EU law on the matter and so drivers in the occasional passenger transport sector find themselves left to their own devices in a grey area. As a result, taxi drivers cannot enjoy the benefits of the single market and entry into the Schengen area. They cannot freely exercise their profession outside of their home country.

Specifically, if a client asks a taxi driver in Croatia to take them to a nearby airport or any other destination in Italy, Austria, Hungary or Slovenia, the driver is legally obliged to leave the client at the border, in order for another taxi driver from that country to pick them up from there. In view of the above: 1.

When is the Commission planning to regulate the participation of taxi drivers at EU level, given the current situation that places taxi drivers at a disadvantage in respect of other professions in the single market?
Does it think that by not regulating passenger transport-on-demand in the EU, it is jeopardising the safety of Europe’s roads?
answer: 1. The Commission currently has no plans to propose legislation at EU level regulating the profession of taxi drivers and/or drivers of Private Hire Vehicles (PHV).

Cross-border services of taxis and PHV constitute only a tiny fraction of all taxi and PHV services provided in the EU and in general conventions exist in border regions which allow the service to end at a destination outside of the Member State of origin.

The Commission is of the opinion that taxi and PHV services should be regulated by Member States provided that the basic general principles of EU law are respected and in particular the freedom of establishment enshrined in Article 49 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (1). 2.
The Commission has no indication to believe that not regulating taxi and PHV services at EU level is jeopardising road safety.
